clue.text: Right to walk at leisure, and go where one pleases

parts.note: to amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace

explanation.surface: A claim to the public right to roam the countryside freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramble is to wander aimlessly, roaming wherever the fancy takes you.

clue.text: With a game point, he puts up a defence

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A player with a match point in hand defends stoutly.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist is someone who argues in defence of a cause or belief.

clue.text: Sword-belt excited ribald comment at first

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order
only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A sword-belt prompts a bawdy remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sword-belt' is a rare word, so the anagram signalled by 'excited' does most of the work, with 'at first' adding the opening of 'comment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt worn over the shoulder to carry a sword.

clue.text: Fairy's ill-gotten gains — a small amount of money extracted

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out of the word for the gains

parts.note: pelf is money gained dishonestly
P is a penny, a small sum

explanation.surface: A fairy's dishonest takings, with a little cash taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small mischievous fairy of folklore.

clue.text: Antipathy to state and people of Israel

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
Sion (Zion) stands for the Jewish people as a whole

explanation.surface: Hostility directed at a country and the Israeli people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; Sion is an old spelling of Zion, used for Israel and its people.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, a synonym of antipathy.

clue.text: Pit gives baby's mother no trouble

indicators.note: the words give up the answer from within their letters

explanation.surface: A mine is causing a new mother no bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysm is an old word for an abyss, a bottomless pit.

clue.text: I get a pen pal in trouble in Braeburn, perhaps

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A correspondent of mine has got into difficulty in a place called Braeburn.
explanation.definitionFit: Braeburn is an example of a dessert apple variety, eaten raw.

clue.text: Severely criticise one initially frightened in spooky surroundings

indicators.note: the spooky word forms surroundings for the other letters

parts.note: spooky means scary
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Someone, scared at first in an eerie setting, lays into another.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarify is to criticise harshly, figuratively scratching the skin.

clue.text: Pat at one time taken round university

indicators.note: the time word is taken round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: once means at one time

explanation.surface: Pat was once given a tour of the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a name; it is the adverb meaning exactly on time, as in 'arrived pat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat as an adverb means at just the right moment, the same as on cue.

clue.text: Place regularly seized by model, so arrogant

indicators.note: something seized by another is held inside it, so the model wraps round the rest

parts.note: a toy is a small model, like a toy car
Pl. is the abbreviation for Place in street addresses
oft is an old word for often, i.e. regularly

explanation.surface: Someone at a model's place keeps grabbing things, which seems rather arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like a signal to take alternate letters of 'Place', but here it means often; 'seized by' puts the place and the often words inside the model word.
explanation.definitionFit: Toplofty is an informal word for haughty or superior, much the same as arrogant.

clue.text: Hair which starts to change hue

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns

indicators.note: the starts of the two following words supply their opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone's hair whose colour is beginning to shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A thatch is a jocular term for a thick head of hair, by analogy with a straw roof.

clue.text: Competent worker takes trip to island"

parts.note: a journey is a trip
Man is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A capable tradesman sets off on a voyage to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a qualified, reliable craftsman who has served an apprenticeship but is not a master.

clue.text: Missionary, very good, brought in to wash up

indicators.note: one word is brought in to the other, going inside it
in a down entry up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to lave is to wash
angelic means very good

explanation.surface: A missionary with a saintly manner is called in to do the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the wash word because this is a down entry; 'brought in' puts the very good word inside it, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelical describes zeal for spreading the gospel, as a missionary does.

clue.text: Thought I had extreme eczema

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A patient remembers suffering a severe case of eczema.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion formed in the mind.

clue.text: Opening up zestfully, I'd never considered it might be galvanising

indicators.note: the openings of the four following words give their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone enthusiastically starts a task they had never thought would be so energising.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanising means coating iron or steel with zinc to stop it rusting.

clue.text: Revelation of a US author about brief topical song

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes round it

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song often commenting on current events

explanation.surface: An American writer's revelation concerning a short song about the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the final letter of the song, and 'about' puts the shortened song inside the author's name; A comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation, the last book of the Bible, is also called the Apocalypse.

clue.text: Public excluded

definitions.meaning: ... as in known to everyone, like a secret that is now open
... as in left outside, not admitted

explanation.definitionFit: Out means revealed to all, and also shut out or eliminated.

clue.text: A different name thereupon applied to fuel

parts.note: so can mean thereupon, as in 'and so he left'
a briquet (briquette) is a block of compressed coal dust used as fuel

explanation.surface: A new label was then put on the fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is a nickname, an alternative name.

clue.text: Really vertical

definitions.meaning: ... as an exclamation means honestly, truly

explanation.definitionFit: Straight up is both slang for honestly and a literal phrase for perpendicular.

clue.text: Embarrassing period in a hospital room

parts.note: WK is the abbreviation for week, a period
a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: A difficult time spent on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means causing embarrassment or unease.

clue.text: Play about black dog shown on small stage

indicators.note: the play word goes about the black one, enclosing it

parts.note: to toy is to play
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A drama involving a black dog seen on a little stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Toby is the dog in Punch and Judy, the traditional British puppet show on a small booth stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Toby is the name of the dog in the Punch and Judy puppet show.

clue.text: Grass adapted from US stock

indicators.note: adapted letters are altered into a different order

explanation.surface: A grass bred from American stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a dense clump of grass.

clue.text: Riverside deposit

definitions.meaning: the land at the edge of a river
to put money into a financial institution for safekeeping

explanation.definitionFit: A bank is the edge of a river, and to bank money is to deposit it.

clue.text: Eager to find love, to one's heart's content

parts.note: agog means eager and excited
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone keen to find love so as to be utterly happy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gogo means in abundance, as much as one wants.

clue.text: Authority has replied to change

indicators.note: the words are told to change, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruling body has sent its response asking for reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership is the position of authority over a group.

clue.text: Join team following a rise

parts.note: ff. is the abbreviation for 'and the following' pages

indicators.note: in a down entry a rise reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Joining a squad after a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns XI to IX; 'following' here is the abbreviation ff., placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix is to attach or join one thing to another.

clue.text: It is pieced together from one of the prophets

definitions.meaning: a picture assembled from small pieces of tile or glass
relating to Moses, the Old Testament prophet and lawgiver

explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a picture of fitted pieces; Mosaic also means relating to Moses.

clue.text: Jack of all trades in truth having round stomach

parts.note: a fact is a truth
O is round in shape
tum is informal for stomach

explanation.surface: A handyman, honestly, has a round belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all sorts of jobs, a general handyman.

clue.text: Fish medical man's seen rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a doc is a doctor, a medical man

explanation.surface: A doctor is seen getting up to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The cod is a common food fish of northern seas.

clue.text: Horribly fat and old, shortly cut out butter and eggs

indicators.note: horribly signals that the following words are mangled into a new order
shortly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it out

explanation.surface: Someone fat and elderly is briefly told to give up butter and eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horribly' rearranges FAT and OLD to TOADFL; 'shortly' cuts AXE to AX. Butter and eggs is a folk name for the plant, not breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter and eggs is a common name for the yellow wildflower also called common toadflax.

clue.text: Information about stunning plane

indicators.note: the information word goes about the stunning one, enclosing it

parts.note: data is information
KO, a knockout, is a stunning blow

explanation.surface: Details about a gorgeous aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas Dakota is a famous transport aeroplane, the DC-3.
